extracted.intended_audience: poets, playwrights, critics, and educated readers of literary criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and critical principles for composing and judging wit, poetry, and theatrical character — emphasizing truth, propriety, simplicity, and naturalness versus artificial devices and fashionable affectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propriety of Thoughts and Words
rubrics_metrics.description: If Wit has truly been defined as a Propriety of Thoughts and Words, then that definition will extend to all sorts of Poetry... Propriety of Thought is that Fancy which arises naturally from the Subject, or which the Poet adapts to it. Propriety of Words is the cloathing of these Thoughts with such Expressions as are naturally proper to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thoughts should arise naturally from the subject (or be plausibly adapted to it); words should fit and clothe those thoughts appropriately. This standard is presented as applying to all poetry and as a foundational test of good taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth as the foundation of Thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth is the first Quality, and, as it were, the foundation of Thought; the fairest is the faultiest, or, rather, those which pass for the fairest, are not really so, if they want this Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate ideas and witty thoughts by whether they are founded on truth; cleverness that lacks truthful foundation is judged faulty. (The page also records a dissenting view that 'Falsehood gives it often all its Grace' to show the debate.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical simplicity over Gothic extravagance
rubrics_metrics.description: These writers... I look upon these writers as Goths in Poetry, who, like those in Architecture, not being able to come up to the beautiful Simplicity of the old Greeks and Romans, have endeavoured to supply its place with all the Extravagancies of an irregular Fancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer the 'beautiful Simplicity' exemplified by classical models; avoid irregular, extravagant fancy that substitutes ornament for true form and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid artificial/contrived devices as substitutes for wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups of literary artifices (anagrams, acrosticks/acrostics, chronograms, lipograms, rebuses, crambo/double rhymes, puns, 'mistake-one-person-for-another' games, and other verbal tricks) populate the Temple of False Wit and produce mere diversion rather than genuine wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These devices are presented as frivolous, mechanical, or clownish substitutes for true wit. Use of such contrivances is marked as characteristic of 'false wit' and liable to reduce the naturalness and moral seriousness of a work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit emerges from resemblance and opposition of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Not only the Resemblance, but the Opposition of Ideas, does very often produce Wit... in several little Points, Turns and Antitheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate analogies, contrasts, turns, and antitheses that naturally arise from the subject to generate genuine wit; these are constructive sources rather than mere verbal tricks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and improvement when borrowing
rubrics_metrics.description: The famous Author of the Art of Love has nothing of his own; he borrows all from a greater Master in his own Profession, and, which is worse, improves nothing which he finds: Nature fails him, and being forced to his old Shift, he has Recourse to Witticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an author borrows from predecessors, he should transform and improve the material rather than merely imitate; failure to do so often leads to forced artifices and reliance on mere witticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge by Reason, Truth, and Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: I shall always make Reason, Truth, and Nature the Measures of Praise and Dispraise; if those are for me, the Generality of Opinion is of no Consequence against me; if they are against me, the general Opinion cannot long support me.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating plays and writings, use reason, truthful representation, and naturalness as primary evaluative standards rather than popularity or current applause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character consistency and moral/natural fitness
rubrics_metrics.description: A fine Gentleman should be honest in his Actions, and refined in his Language... This whole celebrated Piece is a perfect Contradiction to good Manners, good Sense, and common Honesty... there is nothing in it but what is built upon the Ruin of Virtue and Innocence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters, especially those presented as genteel or exemplary, should behave and speak in ways consistent with that portrayal; celebrating characters who trample on decency or virtue is a mark against a work's moral and artistic worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the social influence of theatrical wit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Application of Wit in the Theatre has as strong an Effect upon the Manners of our Gentlemen, as the Taste of it has upon the Writings of our Authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Playwrights should be mindful that theatrical representations shape audience manners and social behavior; wit used irresponsibly on stage can encourage vice or bad manners in society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make gesture and outward manner follow inner thought
rubrics_metrics.description: The true Art in this Case is, To make the Mind and Body improve together; and if possible, to make Gesture follow Thought, and not let Thought be employed upon Gesture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In depicting persons (or in training performers), ensure external manner (speech, gesture, carriage) expresses inner character and thought; avoid mannerisms that are mere surface ornament unconnected to interior life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for solid sense and elegant expression over quibbles
rubrics_metrics.description: Les Petits Esprits... like nothing but the Husk and Rind of Wit, prefer a Quibble, a Conceit, an Epigram, before solid Sense and elegant Expression: These are Mob Readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To please discerning readers and to produce lasting work, prioritize substantial ideas and elegant phrasing rather than cheap conceits, quibbles, or epigrams that only entertain a lower, more numerous readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fashion-driven affectation that misrepresents reality
rubrics_metrics.description: The most improper things we commit in the Conduct of our Lives, we are led into by the Force of Fashion... This Fashion of Sorrow is now become a generous Part of the Ceremonial... Princes are elevated so highly above the rest of Mankind, that it is a presumptuous Distinction to take a Part in Honours done to their Memories, except we have Authority for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique or avoid literary/persona choices that merely mirror social fashions or affectations (e.g., mourning as spectacle) and thus obscure authentic feeling or truth; be wary of surface gestures that serve economy or show rather than genuine expression.
